**Premise correction:** There is no nightly database-cleanup job in this codebase, and no cron scheduler is actually running any jobs.

What I checked:

- `internal/scheduler` (`internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`, `job.go`, `parser.go`, `middleware.go`) exists as a generic, standalone cron-style job-scheduling library (with `New`, `WithTimezone`, `WithMiddleware`, `ParseCronExpression`, etc.), but it is never imported or used anywhere outside its own package — a repo-wide search for `scheduler.` outside `internal/scheduler/` returns zero matches. It isn't referenced from `cmd/memos/main.go` or `server/server.go`, so no job is ever registered or run through it.
- I searched all non-test Go files for `cron` and `cleanup`; the only hits are unrelated code comments (e.g. `store.DeleteMemo handles relation and attachment cleanup` in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:579`, best-effort provisional-user cleanup in `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:76`, and attachment-storage cleanup after user deletion in `server/router/api/v1/user_service.go:447`) — these are inline cleanup steps performed synchronously as part of request handling, not scheduled jobs, and none of them is a "database cleanup" job with a cron schedule.
- The only actual scheduled background job in the server is the S3 presign refresher (`server/runner/s3presign`, wired at `server/server.go:161-171`, running every 12 hours via a `time.Ticker`), which is unrelated to database cleanup and isn't driven by a cron expression at all.

So there's no "nightly" time to report — the described job doesn't exist in this repository.
